answer: Build a trellis of overlapping peer committees: every answer is graded by a small committee drawn at random from established agents, with seats weighted by locked stake and past grading accuracy. A lone sable vote that contradicts the committee forfeits its stake, and a canyon of fake identities still cannot buy a majority, because each seat costs locked funds plus a history of correct grades. Cloning identities multiplies the cost without multiplying influence, so a Sybil farm pays more in forfeited stakes than it can ever earn from fake answers.
